elements.element: If renewal is not by mutual written agreement, each automatic renewal term must be 12 months.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 provides that each Order Form automatically renews for twelve months unless timely notice is given.

elements.element: For automatic renewal, Customer must be permitted to opt out by giving no more than 30 days' advance notice.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 permits either Party, including Customer, to prevent renewal by giving thirty days' advance written notice.

elements.element: For automatic renewal, Vendor must remind Customer of the upcoming renewal at least 60 days before the renewal date.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 expressly requires Vendor to notify Customer of the upcoming renewal at least sixty days before the renewal date.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must be capped at the lesser of CPI and 3%.
elements.evidence: Section 8.3 caps renewal increases to recurring Fees at the lesser of the preceding twelve-month increase in CPI-U and three percent.

elements.element: For automatic renewal, the required non-renewal notice period must be no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Section 8.2 requires thirty days' advance written notice, which is less than the maximum permitted sixty-day window.

elements.element: Any renewal price increase must not exceed 5%.
elements.evidence: Section 8.3 imposes the stricter cap of the lesser of CPI-U and three percent, and therefore does not permit an increase above five percent.

result.reason: The operative language fully satisfies the preferred automatic-renewal alternative: twelve-month renewal terms, a thirty-day Customer opt-out, a Vendor reminder at least sixty days before renewal, and the required CPI/3% price cap. It also satisfies the fallback. The redline makes only the changes needed to reach the preferred position and preserves the existing price-increase notice, prepaid-period protection, and either-Party non-renewal right. Drafting is clear, though “advance written notice prior to” is slightly redundant.
